paper.title: Can Large Language Models Invent Algorithms to Improve Themselves?: Algorithm Discovery for Recursive Self-Improvement through Reinforcement Learning
paper.central_claim: Self-Developing lets an LLM generate model-improvement algorithms as code (model merging), evaluate them, and DPO-train itself on the results; the discovered algorithms outperform human-designed merging algorithms and transfer to other models.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: subagent runtime exposes no receipt to the worker; model identity is the configured claude-kimi type only. Full text incl. Appendices A-F read; discovered-algorithm listings (Fig. 11-28) skimmed except Fig. 11. Scope flagged as weights-boundary.

Searched: the trained component is the factory LLM (LoRA-DPO on weights) and the products are merge functions that produce new model weights (M_t = M_0 + tau_t); the retained non-weight artifact is the generated Python merge function. The loop therefore touches weights at both levels (boundary scope).

evidence.locator: Fig 11 / App C (our reading of the code)
evidence.support_explanation: Reading Fig. 11 for K=3 task vectors (and assuming model_dict order Abel, SciPhi, OpenHermes as in Fig. 3): merged = 0.25*tau_1 + 0.25*mean(tau_2) + 0.5*mean(tau_3), where mean is a row-wise (2-D) or scalar (1-D) broadcast. This is a scaled single task vector plus low-rank offsets, a point outside the 20/40/60% grid used for Task Arithmetic; the gain may therefore reflect an unexplored region of the baseline hyperparameter space rather than a novel merging principle. Static reading only; not run.

Searched all sections: no condition samples algorithms from the untrained factory with an equal 9000-sample budget, no random/evolutionary search over merge functions at matched evaluations, no ablation of replay, thresholds or DPO; Table 2 is the only iteration contrast and is single-run.

Single run per configuration; no seeds, intervals, or significance tests are reported anywhere in the paper; GSM8k test n=1220 and MATH n=4400, so the 0.3-point GSM8k gaps in Table 2 are at the level of 4 questions.

Search effort: roughly 100-300 executable candidates evaluated per iteration (300-900 total) for the LLM versus 27 mixing-ratio combos for Task Arithmetic/TIES; budgets are not matched and the factory training cost is not counted.

signatures.object: The algorithm factory (an LLM initialised from the seed model, weights updated by LoRA-DPO) and its generated Python merge functions; the product is a merged model M_t = M_0 + tau_t.
signatures.information: Factory sees only a fixed prompt with a one-shot merge example (App E); evaluator sees the merged model score on a dev set (100 GSM8k / 600 MATH); no external stronger model.
signatures.operation: Sample N=3000 algorithms per iteration at decaying temperature; filter non-executable/timeouts; apply to M0 task vectors; score on dev; build DPO pairs (top 3% vs bottom 10% plus replayed top-3 of earlier iterations); DPO-train the factory; repeat 3 times.
signatures.output: Merge functions; best merged models (top-15 on dev go to a single test evaluation).
signatures.conditions: Seed openchat-3.5-1210, three Mistral-7B-based candidates, mergekit, math tasks.
signatures.feedback: Dev-set accuracy of the merged model (execution feedback via actually merging and evaluating).
signatures.selection_rule: Percentile thresholds on dev score for preference pairs; top-15 by dev for final test.
signatures.persistence: Factory weights after each DPO round; discovered merge functions (code) retained and reused in transfer to new candidates.
signatures.later_use: Next iteration samples from the updated factory; best algorithms reapplied to new candidate sets without re-optimisation.
signatures.claimed_effect: GSM8k +6 points over seed and +4 over Task Arithmetic; +7.4 over re-optimised Task Arithmetic on new candidates; quality of algorithms improves across iterations.
signatures.failure_boundary: Math only; one model family; later iterations mostly tune coefficients; seed model is not updated in the loop; MATH baseline near floor.

gap.author_gap: Improvement algorithms for LLMs are constrained by human knowledge; prior self-improvement uses self-generated data or feedback and does not learn the improvement strategy; neighbors do not improve the generator and depend on stronger external models.
gap.checked_gap: The two stated limitations of neighbors (generator not improved, external dependency) are specific and checkable against the cited DiscoPOP-style (Lu et al. 2024) and STOP (Zelikman et al. 2023) works, but the paper gives no evidence that either limitation is binding; evolutionary model-merging search and AlphaEvolve are only briefly mentioned.
lineage: Task Arithmetic, TIES, Model Stock (human-designed merging)
Lu et al. 2024 (LLM-discovered preference loss), Zelikman et al. 2023 (STOP), AlphaEvolve (Novikov et al. 2025), Yano et al. 2025 (automatic post-training pipelines)
gap.closest_adjacent: LLM-driven algorithm discovery without generator training (Lu 2024, Zelikman 2023, AlphaEvolve 2025).
gap.residue: Whether training the generator beats simply sampling more from the untrained generator at equal budget is unanswered.
gap.stakes: Automating the discovery of model-improvement algorithms.
gap.method_response: Train the generator by DPO on execution-scored algorithm pairs and reuse the algorithms on new candidates.
gap.remaining_gap: No budget-matched generator-off control; narrow task/model scope; weights are touched.
unresolved: Evolutionary model-merging recipes and other population-search LLM methods are not in the pinned materials; their relation is not checked here.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS preference pairs from execution-verified vs failed trajectories + DPO <-> domain proposer trained by preference optimisation on the measured downstream score of its proposals.
pattern_mapping.required_conditions_or_differences: Domain H27 requires delta-reward relative to the pre-edit state, conditioning per query/task, and a harness artifact; here the reward is the raw dev score of a merged model, the generator is unconditioned (fixed prompt), and the artifact is a weight-space operator.

claims.text: LLM-discovered merge algorithms outperform human-designed algorithms (Task Arithmetic, TIES, Model Stock) on GSM8k and match them on MATH.
claims.setting: Seed openchat-3.5-1210; candidates Abel, OpenHermes, SciPhi; math tasks; lm-eval-harness greedy, 5-shot exact match.
claims.baseline_control: Task Arithmetic/TIES with 20/40/60% grid chosen on dev; Model Stock.
claims.selection_vs_test: Algorithms/models chosen on dev; top-15 test-evaluated once; reported top-3 ranking basis ambiguous.
claims.result_denominator: GSM8k 1220 test, MATH 4400 test; single run.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this seed/candidate set, LLM-generated merge functions reach 76.1 GSM8k vs 71.9 for a 27-point TA grid; MATH is a tie and baseline is near floor; novelty of the merge principle is not established.

claims.text: Training the algorithm factory by iterative DPO improves the quality of generated algorithms across iterations.
claims.selection_vs_test: Dev scores for DPO data; test for iteration-best of dev-selected models.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Dev-score distribution shifts up after DPO; test gains between iterations are small (GSM8k) and uncontrolled.

claims.text: Discovered algorithms transfer to out-of-domain candidate models without re-optimisation (+7.4 over re-optimised Task Arithmetic).
claims.setting: Three new candidate models (WizardMath, Starling, BioMistral).
claims.baseline_control: Task Arithmetic with mixing ratios re-optimised for new candidates.
claims.selection_vs_test: Top-15 chosen on original dev; transfer test top-3 reported.
claims.result_denominator: GSM8k 78.8 vs 71.4 best TA; MATH 2.5 vs 1.2.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Dev-selected merge functions give higher test accuracy on a new candidate triple than a coarse TA grid; transfer across seeds/families/tasks is untested.

claims.text: Recursive self-improvement: the seed model and the algorithm factory improve each other.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Only the factory is iterated; generated algorithms are always applied to M0, so the improved model is not an input to later iterations.

assessment.evidence_level_note: Retained artifact = discovered merge functions, evaluated on a held-out test split and on a new candidate set; improver-level (matched-budget) evidence is absent. Scope boundary: weights are trained and produced.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: LLM-written merge functions selected by dev-score and refined by DPO give higher GSM8k test accuracy than a coarse Task Arithmetic grid for this seed/candidate set and on one transfer set; the contribution of generator training is not isolated.
unresolved: whether discovered algorithms are materially novel (Algorithm A reads like a scaled single task vector)

G.reason: Two concrete neighbor limitations are named, but not shown to be binding; closest neighbors (STOP, DiscoPOP-style, AlphaEvolve, evolutionary merging) are named without contrast experiments.

M.reason: Generate-execute-DPO loop is concrete and plausible; but the loop never feeds improved models back (seed fixed), the reward is raw dev score, and the best algorithms mostly tune coefficients; why training the factory beats sampling more is not argued.

X.reason: Pseudocode, hyperparameters, filters, replay, thresholds and protocol are given and reproducible; limits (math only, family) noted. Missing: selection basis for top-3 reporting, factory prompt fixed, no versioning of algorithm pool beyond top lists.

E.measurement.reason: Standard lm-eval GSM8k/MATH with split dev/test and executable validity check, but seed MATH accuracy 0.5% suggests a format-floor regime and the 76.1 vs 71.9 comparison uses a single run.

E.causality.reason: Only an iteration contrast; no matched-budget generator-off or random-search control; search budget is far larger than the baseline grid; best algorithm resembles a scaled single task vector outside the baseline grid.

E.holdout.reason: Dev-only selection then one test evaluation of 15 models, large test sets, plus a transfer test on new candidate models without re-optimisation; top-3 ranking basis ambiguous, dev small, one benchmark family.

E.statistics.reason: Single run per setting, no intervals; Table 2 differences are within a few test questions on GSM8k; filtering counts for failed candidates are shown in Fig. 9 only for temperature study.

E.cost.reason: Generation counts and A100 use are stated but no GPU-hours, no cost of DPO, and baseline gets 27 evaluations vs hundreds of executed candidates.

status_reason: Full text read. Kept in scope as a boundary case because the retained non-weight artifact (executable merge algorithms) is evaluated and transferred; the loop also trains factory weights and outputs weights, so control may overrule.
rationale: Reproducible generate-score-DPO loop with dev/test split and transfer test; but no budget-matched generator-off control, single run, best algorithm looks like a scaled task vector outside the baseline grid, seed not fed back. Weights boundary.
